TABLE.NAME: bento
TABLE.COMMENT: Each row is one Bento presentation activity instance

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Activity name shown on the course page

FIELD.NAME: document
FIELD.COMMENT: The teacher's own bento/slides JSON document — LONGTEXT-equivalent, can hold embedded images. Still the ONLY document when allowstudentsubmissions is off; otherwise it's the teacher's own copy (e.g. an example/instructions deck) while students each get their own row in bento_submissions instead.

FIELD.NAME: grade
FIELD.COMMENT: Max points for the gradebook item; 0 = ungraded; negative = a scale id (standard Moodle convention)

FIELD.NAME: allowstudentsubmissions
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = classic single teacher-authored deck (v1 behaviour). 1 = each enrolled student creates/imports and edits their OWN presentation instead (bento_submissions).

FIELD.NAME: submissionvisibility
FIELD.COMMENT: Only meaningful when allowstudentsubmissions=1. 'auto' = every student can see every other student's submission immediately. 'moderated' = a submission is only visible to OTHER students once a teacher approves it (see bento_submissions.status); the owner can always see/edit their own regardless.

FIELD.NAME: duedate
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = no deadline. Once passed, a student (mod/bento:submit, no mod/bento:edit) can no longer save changes to their own submission — enforced in edit.php and the mod_bento_save_document web service, both server-side. Never restricts mod/bento:edit.

FIELD.NAME: duedatevisible
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the deadline itself (not just its enforcement) is shown to students on the gallery page.

FIELD.NAME: loginonly
FIELD.COMMENT: Restricts the TEACHER's own master presentation to logged-in users even in a course that otherwise allows guest access. Student submissions (bento_submissions) are always login-only regardless of this flag — that restriction is unconditional, enforced directly in the pages that serve them, not tied to a per-instance setting at all.

TABLE.NAME: bento_grades
TABLE.COMMENT: One manually-entered grade per student per bento instance

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student this grade is for

FIELD.NAME: published
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = draft, entered but hidden from the student (grade_grade.hidden=1 in the real gradebook too). 1 = published — visible to the student, same as classic mod_bento grading. Entering/changing a grade never publishes it by itself; only the explicit publish action does.

INDEX.NAME: bentoid-userid
INDEX.COMMENT: One grade row per student per instance

TABLE.NAME: bento_submissions
TABLE.COMMENT: One student-authored bento/slides document per student per instance — only used when bento.allowstudentsubmissions=1

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student who owns this submission — the only user allowed to edit it

FIELD.NAME: document
FIELD.COMMENT: The student's own bento/slides JSON document

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 'pending' (awaiting teacher approval — only relevant in 'moderated' visibility mode) or 'approved'. Ignored entirely in 'auto' visibility mode, where every submission is visible regardless of this value.

INDEX.NAME: bentoid-userid
INDEX.COMMENT: Exactly one submission per student per instance — they keep revising the same row, never create a second one

TABLE.NAME: bento_agreements
TABLE.COMMENT: Records that a user has agreed to the plugin's own terms-of-use text (see the 'termsofuse' admin setting) — site-wide, not per-course/instance, since the terms themselves are a single site-wide setting. Checked before any of view.php/edit.php/submission.php/submission_new.php serve their actual content whenever termsofuse is non-empty; skipped entirely when it's empty (no terms configured means nothing to agree to).

FIELD.NAME: termshash
FIELD.COMMENT: sha1 of the termsofuse text at the moment of agreeing — if the admin later edits the wording, this stops matching the CURRENT setting's own hash and the user is asked to agree again, with no manual version number for anyone to remember to bump.

INDEX.NAME: userid_uix
INDEX.COMMENT: One agreement record per user — re-agreeing overwrites the row rather than inserting a second one
